newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel closes for Yom Kippur.
newsitem.headline: Israel closes for Yom Kippur.

text.p: Israel shut down on Sunday for the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, closing its international borders after having already sealed off the nearly two million Palestinians of the Gaza Strip and West Bank.
Sirens wailed at sunset to mark the start of the Day of Atonement when Jews ask for God's forgiveness by fasting and praying for 25 hours.
Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai warned Syria, which attacked Israel with Egypt 23 years ago on the same holy day, that the Jewish state was strong enough to meet any challenge.
He was reflecting recent Israeli concern at Syrian troop movements in Lebanon.
"We have no interest in a war with Syria, rather in real negotiations with them, that they should be as intensive as they can be," Mordechai told Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth daily.

"And permit me to pass via you a warning to Syria and to Assad: Mr Syrian President, the State of Israel and its security forces are strong and able to fulfil their goals. On that I have not a speck of doubt. My advice to you is: Come, let us go a different path," he added.
President Hafez al-Assad's redeployment of about a third of his 35,000 troops in Lebanon caused war jitters in Israel although Western military analysts said the fears seemed unfounded.
The Syrian-Egyptian attack on Yom Kippur 1973 caught Israel off guard. The country grinds to a halt for the fast. No traffic moves on streets, businesses close, and all broadcasts stop.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, elected on a right-wing platform in May, called for the healing of divisions among Jews which split Israel after the assassination by a right-wing Jew of Labour Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin last November.

"On this day we remember that our power depends on the unity of the people and not its division, on love of Israel and not in hatred of brothers, in mutual understanding and not on violent decisions such as the one that cut off the life of our late Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, may he rest in peace, in the disastrous last year," Netanyahu said in the last broadcast before the radio went off the air.
